title: Rigidity and common-cover comparison of log blowup towers
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and $u:(U,N)\to(X,M)$ a surjective strict etale morphism [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup, def-weil-etale-morphism]. For two ideal subsheaves $I,J\subset M$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], equality of their restrictions to $U$ implies $I=J$; explicitly $m\in I(V)$ if and only if its restriction to $V\times_XU$ belongs to $I|_U$ for every etale $V\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product].

Let $B,C$ be two finite saturated log blowup towers over $X$, with nonempty coherent ordered centers [def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure]. Any ordered isomorphism $u^*B\simeq u^*C$ of their uncontracted pullbacks, identity on $U$ and preserving the actual centers, is the pullback of a unique such isomorphism $B\simeq C$. There is at most one ordered center-preserving isomorphism $B\simeq C$ over the identity of $X$. Consequently equalities and cocycle identities between such isomorphisms can be tested after a surjective strict etale cover.

In particular, let $U\to X$ and $V\to X$ be two surjective strict etale covers, let $S$ and $T$ be contracted finite towers over $U$ and $V$ with center-preserving uncontracted descent data, and let $B,C$ be towers descending these data. If the full pullbacks of $S,T$ to $U\times_XV$ are isomorphic over the identity with centers and order preserved, then $B,C$ have the same length and are uniquely isomorphic over $X$ with centers preserved. For three such choices the resulting comparisons satisfy the cocycle identity. Descent using the identity cover of a charted input returns the original tower with its actual centers.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110: uniqueness in the descent reduction and comparison on a finite common cover, expanded using 3.3.8--3.3.10.

proof.text: For an etale $V\to X$, put $V_U=V\times_XU$. The etale-cover base-change lemma, applied to the singleton cover $U\to X$, makes $V_U\to V$ a cover. Since $u$ is strict etale, restriction of its log structure and of a subideal to the small site of $U$ is ordinary sheaf restriction. If $m|_{V_U}\in I(V_U)$, its two restrictions agree on $V_U\times_VV_U$ as sections of $M$, hence as sections of the subsheaf $I$. The sheaf equalizer for $I$ glues them to $a\in I(V)$; separatedness of $M$ gives $a=m$. The converse is restriction. Apply this membership criterion to both $I,J$ to obtain equality whenever their restrictions agree. The argument works for every ideal subsheaf, without coherence.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10, pp.107--108; proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, descent and uniqueness reductions.

proof.text: First prove uniqueness without a cover. Two ordered center-preserving tower isomorphisms have the same initial log morphism, the identity. Suppose their level-$i$ maps agree. Their level-$(i+1)$ maps have target the universal saturated log blowup of the center on the target level $i$. They factor the same log morphism from the source level $i+1$, and that morphism pulls this center back to the invertible blown-up ideal, because the level-$i$ map preserves the actual center. The uniqueness clause of the blowup universal property makes the two maps equal, including their log-section maps. Induction proves uniqueness at every level. This uses finite ordered towers, with the length-zero case given by the identity.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10, pp.107--108; proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, descent and uniqueness reductions.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:u^*B\simeq u^*C$ be the given isomorphism of uncontracted towers. Their lengths agree, since uncontracted pullback keeps the ordered stage set. At each level the synchronization lemma identifies the full pullback of $B$ with $U_i=U\times_X B_i$, and $U_i\to B_i$ is surjective strict etale. Set $\phi_0=1_X$. Maintain the induction hypothesis that $\phi_i:B_i\simeq C_i$ has been constructed and its pullback is $\alpha_i$. Transport the center of $C_i$ to an ideal on $B_i$ by $\phi_i$. Its restriction to $U_i$ equals the center of $B_i$ restricted there, since $\alpha_i$ preserves actual centers. Step 1 on $B_i$ therefore identifies these ideals on $B_i$. No contraction, and no inference from equality of the resulting blowup spaces alone, is used.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10, pp.107--108; proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, descent and uniqueness reductions.

proof.text: Using the center equality just obtained, the log morphism $B_{i+1}\to B_i\xrightarrow{\phi_i}C_i$ pulls the center of $C_i$ back to an invertible ideal. The universal property of $C_{i+1}$ gives its unique lift $\phi_{i+1}:B_{i+1}\to C_{i+1}$. Applying the same construction to $\phi_i^{-1}$ gives a reverse lift. Their composites factor the original blowup arrows over the identities, so uniqueness identifies both composites with the identity. Thus $\phi_{i+1}$ is a log isomorphism. Its pullback and $\alpha_{i+1}$ factor the same log morphism through the pulled-back blowup of the same center, so uniqueness also identifies them. This advances the induction, including the prescribed local map, not just its underlying scheme map.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10, pp.107--108; proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, descent and uniqueness reductions.

proof.text: Finite induction in steps 3--4 constructs the required ordered isomorphism $B\simeq C$, and step 2 makes it unique. The next induction stage checks preservation of each center; all arrows commute by the factorization equations. In particular two candidate ordered center-preserving maps agree globally; any equality, including a cocycle equation between composites of such isomorphisms, holds if it holds on the cover (indeed both sides already agree by step 2). This proves both the lifting assertion and the stated equality test.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10, pp.107--108; proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, descent and uniqueness reductions.

proof.text: For the last clause put $W=U\times_XV$. The etale-cover base-change lemma makes $W\to U$ a surjective etale cover. Give $W$ the log structure obtained by restricting $M$; strictness identifies it with the restriction from either $U$ or $V$, so this cover is strict. The specified full identifications $u^*B\simeq S$, $v^*C\simeq T$ and the common-cover isomorphism give an isomorphism between the full pullbacks of $u^*B$ and $u^*C$ to $W$; recursive pullbacks associate by the fibre-product universal property, and at each blowup by its unique factorization. Apply steps 3--5 first to $W\to U$, then to $U\to X$. The result is the unique isomorphism $B\simeq C$, with equal lengths. Any compatibility with the specified descent data holds by step 2 on the overlaps: both sides are ordered center-preserving isomorphisms over the identity. The same uniqueness gives the cocycle for three choices. For the identity cover the original tower itself realizes the data, and the resulting comparison with any descended tower preserves its actual centers, giving the final assertion.
